(2) Write docs/iadm/IADM01_PHASE0_REPORT.md: per blueprint item EXISTS or NEW, tagged CONFIRMED / INFERRED / NOT FOUND; table-name map; permission-key map; route-collision check with /api/v1/admin/**; list of gaps that need a migration. title: Durable audit on every mutation
story: As an auditor, I can trust that every IADM-01 change is recorded, so no change is ever reported as successful without an audit entry.
screen_or_desk: Visible later in Ops & Audit Search
acceptance_criteria: (1) Every mutation writes a shared-audit entry with actor, action (IADM01_* names below), resource, institute scope, reason where required, correlation id and timestamp. (2) Success is returned only after the audit record is durable (same transaction or an approved outbox); if it cannot be recorded, the mutation does not succeed and the admin sees a clear message. (3) No local duplicate audit store. (4) Test: audit unavailable means no successful mutation.
permission_key_hint: n/a
denied_and_negative_tests: Simulate an audit write failure: the mutation is rolled back and reported as failed.
demo_checklist_step: Every mutating step
status_demo: DONE - IADM01_* rows in audit.events for S1F
notes: Earlier audit work found two audit tables (a change log and an events table). Phase 0 must confirm which one the audit search reads and which one the triggers write to, so a new entry is actually found by search.

title: Institute isolation and permission baseline
story: As the platform, an institute is the isolation boundary and every IADM-01 call is checked by permission key and scope, so no one sees or changes another institute.
screen_or_desk: None
acceptance_criteria: (1) Tenant = Institute; a college belongs to one institute and is never a tenant. (2) Every query is scoped by institute; the database session runs as the non-privileged role so row-level security applies; Java checks and RLS both enforce scope. (3) Authorization uses permission keys, never role names. (4) Missing or ambiguous scope fails closed. (5) Allowed and denied tests for every endpoint group and each actor.
permission_key_hint: Candidate (from RBAC audit; VERIFY in Phase 0): adm01.* family = institute and tenant lifecycle (manage/write/view). Do not invent or rename keys.
denied_and_negative_tests: Institution Admin (R03) of institute A cannot read or change institute B; College Admin (R04) is denied every IADM-01 institute operation; Auditor (R28) cannot call any mutating endpoint.
demo_checklist_step: Negative checks
status_api: PARTIAL - permission keys + platform admin; live R03 cross-tenant suite pending
status_demo: PARTIAL - R04 BFF deny 403; fuller deny suite pending
notes: Never accept a caller-supplied institute id as proof of scope.

title: Invite or create the first Institution Admin's login
story: As Super Admin, I can invite the first Institution Admin by email so the person gets a real login before any profile or role exists.

title: Full export request and approval (workflow only)

title: Read-only view of institutes and lifecycle history
story: As Auditor, I can view institutes, colleges and their lifecycle history without being able to change anything.
screen_or_desk: Auditor read-only area (institute list, detail, audit trail)
acceptance_criteria: (1) Auditor sees institutes, colleges, handover records and lifecycle history within the assigned scope. (2) No create, update, approve or execute control is shown. (3) Every mutating endpoint refuses the Auditor. (4) The Auditor holds no audit-administration key.

title: Lifecycle history and audit trail for an institute
story: As an administrator or auditor, I can see who did what to an institute and when, so changes are accountable.
screen_or_desk: Institute detail > Audit trail tab; Ops & Audit Search
acceptance_criteria: (1) Timeline of lifecycle entries (registered, appointed, college created, handover, requested, decided, suspended, reactivated, archived) with actor, reason and time. (2) A new action appears within seconds in the trail and in audit search (test registers an institute and then finds it). (3) R03 sees own institute only. (4) No edit or delete path.
